title: Animal Adaptations
hook: A camel's hump, a chameleon's color, a polar bear's fat — these aren't accidents. Each is a trait shaped over generations to fit a particular way of life.
key_points: An adaptation is an inherited trait that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its environment.
Adaptations arise over many generations through natural selection.
They can be physical (body parts) or behavioral (things an animal does).
Adaptations fit an animal to its niche — its particular role and place in an ecosystem.
content_html: Look closely at any animal and you'll find its body and habits seem tailored to where it lives. A camel stores fat in its hump for the desert, a polar bear carries a thick insulating layer for the Arctic, a chameleon shifts color to hide. These fitting features are adaptations.
extra_html: An adaptation is an inherited trait that improves an animal's chances of surviving and reproducing in its environment. It isn't something an individual chooses or grows on demand; it emerges over many generations through natural selection, as the traits that help most become more common in a population. Adaptations come in two flavors: physical ones, like a hawk's sharp talons or gills for breathing underwater, and behavioral ones, like birds migrating ahead of winter or wolves hunting in packs. Together they fit each animal to its niche — its particular role and place within an ecosystem. Encyclopaedia Britannica's article on adaptation explains how these traits arise and why they match animals so neatly to their surroundings.

related.title: The Animal Kingdom
related.hook: Sponges, spiders, sharks, and squirrels look nothing alike — yet all are animals, sharing a few deep traits that set them apart from plants, fungi, and microbes.

related.title: How Animals Behave
related.hook: A spider spins a perfect web without a lesson, while a crow figures out a new trick by trial and error — two sides of how animals act in the world.

related.title: Food Chains & Energy Flow
related.hook: Energy enters most ecosystems as sunlight, gets captured by plants, and flows up the menu — but it leaks away at every bite, so the chain stays short.

flashcards.back_html: An inherited trait that helps an organism survive and reproduce in its environment. It can be physical (a body part) or behavioral (something the animal does).

choices.text: Over many generations through natural selection
An animal decides to grow them within its own lifetime
They appear instantly whenever the weather changes

flashcards.explanation_html: Adaptations aren't chosen by an individual. Helpful inherited traits make survival and reproduction more likely, so they become more common over many generations.

flashcards.prompt: Which of these is a behavioral adaptation rather than a physical one?

choices.text: Birds migrating south for the winter
A polar bear's thick layer of fat

flashcards.explanation_html: Migration is something the animal does — a behavioral adaptation. Body fat and color-changing skin are physical traits.
